interpretation: Evidence channels are heterogeneous with respect to the ecological target: eliminating more worlds is not equivalent to changing the reachability envelope.
Temporal arrival-order evidence never changed the robust-impossibility envelope in any eligible row, even though it contracted world identity in 70 rows.
Barrier-state and analyst-rule evidence were the most frequent envelope-changing channels in the frozen panel.
Source identity primarily refined exact reachability target classes and only occasionally changed robust impossibility.
Target-specific evidence burden never exceeded full-world burden and was strictly smaller in 97/272 eligible rows.
The original EOG evidence-design question should therefore be framed relative to the target boundary a measurement can cross, not simply how many worlds it eliminates.
claim_boundary: Direct source/barrier/analyst channels are known-truth diagnostic measurements, not assertions of field measurability.
Unit evidence-channel count is not monetary or logistical field cost.
Reachability-class identification does not identify historical truth.
The channel-effect frequencies are properties of the frozen directed candidate-world generator.
